summary: Ingress header clipping truncates Authorization bearer token for private deployment, causing 401 errors
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 401s from the Redwood private API for requests proxied through their on-prem ingress. Impact: Customer's production integration cannot complete inference calls; errors began after a recent rollout that added a long service-account assertion header. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed control plane), prod, us-east-1. Observed behavior: Requests that include a long Authorization header (service-to-service bearer token which includes a long nested JWT) receive 401 Unauthorized from the identity-proxy. The token appears truncated in the proxy logs. Expected behavior: Identity proxy should forward the full Authorization header to the auth service and validate the token, returning 200 for valid tokens. Workaround: Short-term workaround was to reduce the size of the assertion header (customer-side) and use token introspection endpoint for smaller tokens.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private deployment with customer ingress (NGINX/HAProxy) that proxies requests to Redwood identity-proxy. 2) Attach an Authorization header containing a long bearer token (>8192 bytes) produced by the customer's token service (includes nested claims). 3) Send standard generate/chat request to Redwood API route. 4) Observe 401 response and identity-proxy logs showing 'Authorization header truncated' or token decode error.
logs:
identity-proxy[2026-03-10T14:22:10Z] ERROR token_validation.go:86 invalid token: token parsing failed: unexpected EOF
nginx[2026-03-10T14:22:09Z] upstream sent invalid response while reading response header from upstream
-- captured truncated header (authorization): 'Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6Ij...' (length reported: 4096)
-- original token length reported by customer: 12048 bytes
comments: 2026-03-10 | Support (Maya): Opened ticket after initial CS report. Requested full proxy config, ingress type, and sample failing request headers. Asked for test token and timestamp of failures.
2026-03-10 | Customer (Aurelia Eng, Jordan): Provided nginx.conf snippet and sample token. Noted failures started after their auth pump that appended long trace metadata to assertions.

2026-03-10 | SRE (Daniel): Reproduced locally using customer's token shape. Observed header truncated by nginx default buffer size. Added hypothesis: ingress is dropping/truncating headers exceeding buffer limits, leading to corrupted tokens reaching identity-proxy.

2026-03-11 | Eng (SRE): Validated that identity-proxy can accept large headers (no hardcoded limit), upstream proxies are the culprit. Opened PR to docs and runbook recommending ingress config and updated onboarding checklist for private customers.

2026-03-12 | Support (Maya): Confirmed with customer that after adjusting nginx proxy_buffer_size and proxy_busy_buffers_size per recommended values and removing appended metadata, requests are succeeding. Customer validated end-to-end traffic in prod with no 401s for >24h.
investigation_notes: Checked identity-proxy codepath: no arbitrary header length cap found; decoding libraries return EOF when token truncated.
Reproduced with a local nginx using default large_client_header_buffers (8k per buffer). Token >8k leads to truncation in proxy_pass path.
SRE test: increased nginx large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffer_size to 32k, and upstream requests succeed.
Observed error pattern distinct from JWKS rotation or SAML issues: token was malformed due to truncation rather than signature mismatch.
Customer ingress earlier had a vendor default that strips header segments after a specific byte length; vendor docs confirmed this behavior for legacy builds.
Related internal ticket INT-4321 created to add an ingress checklist item and automated verification for private customer deploys to detect unsafe header truncation defaults.
resolution: Root cause: Customer's ingress (NGINX with vendor defaults) was configured with insufficient header buffer sizes which resulted in Authorization header truncation for very large bearer tokens. Remediation: 1) Provided documented recommended ingress settings (large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffer_size >= token size). 2) Customer removed non-essential metadata appended to tokens and switched to compressed token format for long assertions. 3) Added runbook entry to private-deployment onboarding: verify ingress header buffer limits and run a synthetic request with oversized token. 4) Internal follow-up INT-4321 to add an automated check in deployment scripts.
follow_up_actions: Add ingress header sizing verification to private deployment checklist
Update onboarding docs and sample nginx config
Ship automated test that sends oversized token during smoke tests
customer_communication_summary: Explained issue root cause (ingress header buffer limits) and provided step-by-step mitigation. Customer implemented recommended nginx config changes and validated success. Customer accepted the fix and requested the updated docs be added to their onboarding checklist.
